literal: Than incurring the enmity of many people, abandoning the friendship of the good is ten-fold harmful.
translation: Abandoning the friendship of the wise and good is ten times more harmful than incurring the enmity of many foes.
modern: பலருடைய பகையைத் தேடிக்கொள்வதை விட, நல்லவர்களின் நட்பைக் கைவிடுவது பத்து மடங்கு அதிகத் தீமையைத் தரும்.
explanation: This couplet highlights the vital importance of retaining the support of wise and virtuous guides. The poet compares two undesirable situations: earning the hostility of many people and losing the friendship of the good. He declares that abandoning (விடல்) the association (தொடர்கை) of the wise (நல்லார்) is ten times (பத்தடுத்த) more ruinous (தீமைத்தே) than making many enemies (பல்லார் பகை). Without the guidance of the wise, one is left completely vulnerable to errors, making the loss of their friendship far more dangerous than any external opposition.
